report:
Reviewed the full local_identity claim and all sixteen implementation associations across thirteen local-symbol files, all four executable associated tests, and the explicit TODO test. Requirements are definition-based identity; independent CST/span/signature/member/body detail; identity preservation after detail edits; reuse for unchanged sibling facts; and distinguishable real identity changes.

Functions, consts and type aliases identify by name/scope/associated owner while CST and span are tracked detail. Structs, enums, traits and statics likewise keep name/scope distinct from tracked CST/span. Modules retain name/edition/parent identity, with body_source, attrs and span as tracked detail. Uses, macro invocations and impls carry scope identity with imports/CST/span separately tracked; macro definitions retain name/scope and independently tracked attrs/body tokens/span. Variants use name and parent-enum identity while CST/span/is_tuple are tracked; constructors use name and variant identity. Associated-item helpers use owner plus kind/name/occurrence, then reconstruct CST and span behind the keyed query boundary, so inserting/reordering a differently named sibling does not change the target's key. Separate signature/items/body operations are downstream queries keyed by these symbols rather than fields in their identity. The new import diagnostics and symbol_local_item helper only inspect existing identities/provenance and introduce no new identity field or constructor.

Captured parser constructors pass stable name/scope/owner values separately from reconstructed CST/spans; captured Symbol conversion retains local handles. Captured Scope/LocalAssociatedOwner definitions establish owner identity. Captured setup_root_module reconstructs a root in a tracked context and specifies parsed children. ObservedSymbol interns only Symbol, and observe_symbol_identity is a tracked no-detail query; Database records WillExecute events, so asserting the observer did not reexecute after reconstruction tests key reuse rather than comparing display strings.

The per-kind detail test explicitly exercises twelve local kinds, rejects parse-error substitutes, checks an unchanged warm trace, edits source and asserts no identity-observer execution. The enum test forces variant and constructor observers before/after a field-type edit. The identity-change test verifies cold observation, rename-triggered observer execution, and distinct same-name definitions in distinct scopes. The associated-item test covers insertion and reordering for functions/types/consts under both traits and impls, checks owner links, and checks no target observer execution in both edit directions. These test assertions would detect accidental CST/span inclusion in identity for those scenarios. They do not prove the full per-kind sibling signature/member/body reuse matrix: todo::symbols_local_identity explicitly retains sibling insertion/reordering and signature/member/body reuse for every local kind as deferred work. Completing it requires observers of each independent fact, not simply adding more successful compilations. No N/A evidence exists.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib query_keys: 4 passed, including the three associated query-key tests and one unrelated matched test. Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib local_function_identity_changes_are_distinguishable: 1 passed. These runs complement, not replace, the above source assessment. No production edits were made and no new identity violation found. Existing TODO remains visible; no requested edits.
